Evaluations

You buy a challenge, pass it, and are then handed a funded account under a different contract. The two drawdown and consistency columns are the two stages — where they differ is where the money goes. Cost to funded is the full bill: first attempt, every repeat, and the activation fee, with each factor in its own column. Click any header to sort.

How to play it

One trade a day. The day target is the profit target divided by the winning days the consistency rule forces (ceil(1 / consistency)). The bet is the legal bet with the highest simulated no-edge pass rate — every candidate the contract's own numbers suggest (the stated daily loss limit, the drawdown and its halves, thirds and quarters, and the 1.5R point) is simulated and the winner shown; hover P(pass) to see them all. Bigger legal bets usually pass more, because the end-of-day trailing drawdown ratchets less when you take fewer, larger steps. This is a sizing rule, not an edge claim — every number here assumes profit factor 1.0, a book with no edge at all.

Instant funded

No evaluation to pass and nothing to reset: you pay once and trade a funded account under the rules shown. There is no eval stage, so those columns are absent rather than blank, and "cost to funded" is simply the price plus any activation fee — the attempt count does not apply. Hidden by default (the "Include instant-funded" chip switches them on); never part of the EV ranking.

Promos

Flash discounts caught by the promo watcher on the firms' own pages. A standing permanent sale is never a flash promo — eleven firms run one year-round, so the struck-through price is fiction.

What this page assumes

Cost model
  • A code is only as good as its verification. Codes are ranked confidence-first, so a verified 40% is preferred over an unverified 90%.
  • Where is_permanent_sale is true the list price is marketing; the street price IS the price and the headline discount percentage is meaningless.
  • repeat_attempt_usd is the honest driver of total spend. Most firms exclude resets from codes, so attempts 2..N cost full price.
  • On monthly firms a promo normally covers the first month only, and several failed attempts inside one paid month cost one fee.
  • An unread fee stays null and is labelled, never defaulted to $0. activation_usd, reset_usd and billing each carry a *_stated flag; where one says not_shown the cost-to-funded total states the reading it used.
  • Cost to funded (one-time billing) = first attempt + (attempts − 1) × repeat + activation.
  • Cost to funded (monthly billing) = first month + (months − 1) × rebill + (attempts − 1) × reset + activation, where months = ceil(attempts × mean sessions per attempt / 21).
  • attempts = 1 / P(pass) at the playbook sizing. Attempts are treated as independent.
Playbook and P(pass)
  • P(pass) is the NO-EDGE null: profit factor 1.0, one trade a day, win rate 1/(1+R:R). It prices the CONTRACT, not the trader, and is not a forecast.
  • No firm in this dataset states an evaluation deadline. evalsim cannot take a null deadline, so a 252-session horizon stands in for one. An attempt still unresolved at the horizon is counted as a failure.
  • Per-trade cost is 0: a profit factor of 1.0 is already net of the trader's own commissions, and charging them again double-counts.
  • A daily loss limit is treated as ending the day, not the account, and is a bet candidate only when the firm STATES it.
  • Monthly-billed plans are charged 21 sessions to the month, using the simulated mean sessions per attempt over pass AND fail paths.
EV (null) column
  • Best zero-edge EV over 25 null cells (5 R:R x 5 risk sizes): EV = -fee + P(pass) x E[$ first payout | funded]. Fee = the cost model's first-attempt price while the code is valid. Funded stage on the firm's own payout rules where researched (badge 'rules'), else the Topstep-XFA template. Ranking, not a forecast - see the EV assumptions panel.
  • EV = -price_after_discount + P(pass) * E[$ delivered | funded]
  • Trades are IID draws from (win_rate, rr). Real books are autocorrelated and path-dependent, and a barrier problem is very sensitive to that, so treat the grid as a ranking tool over rule geometry, NOT as a forecast of your P&L.
  • A daily loss limit is modelled as ending the day, not the account. If a firm hard-fails on a DLL breach its true P(pass) is LOWER than shown.
  • Where a firm publishes no payout cap, the request is modelled as the firm's own drawdown amount.
  • Where a withdrawal buffer is published, payout policy is 'threshold' at buffer + cap, which forbids smaller legal withdrawals and is conservative.
  • Eval fee is charged ONCE. For monthly-subscription firms (Topstep, TradeDay, most MFF plans) several failed attempts inside one paid month cost one fee, so their EV here is understated.
  • trades_per_day is fixed at 3 at both stages (a 1-trade/day funded variant is not evaluated).
  • Funded stage: plans with an entry in funded_payout_rules.json (funded_rules='rules_file') are priced on that firm's own first-payout rules; all others use the v2 Topstep-XFA template (50% of balance, min_days_to_payout as winning days >= $0.01, floor locked at start, take_first unless a buffer is published) and are flagged funded_rules='default_topstep_template'. The two groups are NOT like-for-like.
  • Rules-file plans: the trader's payout POLICY is chosen per cell as the better E[$] of take_first (first day the firm's gates allow, incl. min cycle profit) and wait_for_max_request (balance >= buffer + cap / withdrawable_fraction). Both use the same seed (CRN). Intermediate thresholds are not searched, so E[$] is a lower bound on the best threshold policy.
  • Only the FIRST payout is valued. Later payouts, 30-day fraction unlocks, floor_after_withdrawal and max-payouts-before-close are recorded in the rules file but not simulated; firms whose value is mostly in later payouts are understated.
  • With withdrawable_fraction >= 1 and a floor locked above start, the request is bounded by the lock offset (withdrawing through the floor is a hard breach).
  • Funded max_contracts is the plan's own limit but is inert: the engine does not cap the dollar bet by contracts while cost_usd = 0.
  • Rows marked stale had a price or rule change after their cells were simulated; re-run build/ev_grid.py (resumable) then build/rank_eval_plans.py.
